gloss.intro: The words developers (and the AI teams) use, in plain English.
gloss.switch.help: Dotted words get a plain explanation when you hover them.
gloss.backlog.text: Ideas and work not planned in yet. Nothing there gets worked on until it moves to To do.
gloss.sprint.text: A short stretch of work (often a week or two) with an agreed set of cards to finish.
gloss.standup.text: A quick check-in: what each team member did, what they do next, and what is stopping them.
gloss.bug.text: Something that doesn’t work the way it should.
gloss.test.text: Trying a finished piece of work to check it does what was asked, before you accept it.
gloss.commit.text: A saved snapshot of the code, with a short note of what changed. You can always go back to one.
gloss.push.text: Sending saved snapshots (commits) from this computer up to GitHub, so they are backed up and shared.
gloss.branch.text: A separate line of work in the code, so changes can be made without touching the main version.
gloss.merge.text: Joining a branch’s changes back into the main version.
gloss.repo.text: The project’s folder of code and its full history of commits, usually also kept on GitHub.
gloss.refactor.text: Tidying the code without changing what it does: smaller files, clearer names, less repetition.
gloss.deploy.text: Putting a new version live, for example onto a server where people use it.
gloss.kanban.text: A board with columns (To do, In progress, Done) where cards move left to right as work happens.
gloss.wip.text: Work in progress: the most cards a column should hold, so the team finishes things before starting more.
gloss.pr.text: Asking for a branch’s changes to be checked and merged into the main version.
gloss.hook.text: A small command that runs by itself at a set moment, e.g. when an AI session starts, so the team hears your comments.
gloss.token.text: The unit AI usage is counted in: roughly a few letters of text read or written. Fewer tokens, more of your plan left.
gloss.agent.text: An AI that works on its own on a task: reads the code, makes changes, runs checks, and reports back.
tour.btn.title: A short guided tour of the board
tour.intro: A few stops around the board. How much do you want?
tour.lvl.new.help: Every stop, and why it works this way. Developer words get explained too.
tour.lvl.refresh.help: The main stops, in a line each.
tour.welcome.title: Welcome to AI-gile
tour.welcome.text: A board where AI teams do the work and you decide, test and accept. Here is how to find your way around.
tour.welcome.short: A quick lap of the board.
tour.welcome.why: The idea: the teams do the busywork, and you only see what needs a human.
tour.rail.title: Your projects
tour.rail.text: Home, your inbox, chats with the leads, then one icon per project. A purple diamond means something there is waiting on you. Drag icons to put them in your order.
tour.rail.short: Projects on the left; purple diamonds mean something waits on you.
tour.rail.why: One glance tells you where you are needed, without opening anything.
tour.inbox.title: Your inbox
tour.inbox.text: Everything waiting on you, across every project: questions, to-dos only you can do, and things to test. Click a chip to see just that kind.
tour.inbox.short: All that waits on you, everywhere. Click a chip for one kind.
tour.inbox.why: You shouldn’t have to visit every project to know what needs you.
tour.foryou.title: For you
tour.foryou.text: On a board, this column holds what waits on you in that project. Open a test, follow its steps, then Accept or Send back with a reason.
tour.foryou.short: This project’s pile for you: test, then Accept or Send back.
tour.foryou.why: Teams never mark their own work done: you accept it. That keeps quality in your hands.
tour.cards.title: The teams’ columns
tour.cards.text: The rest of the board is the teams’ work: Backlog, To do, In progress and so on. Comment on any card and the team wakes up to deal with it.
tour.cards.short: The teams’ work. Comment on a card to wake them.
tour.cards.why: Your comments are instructions. The board starts the team when you write.
tour.chat.title: Chat with the leads
tour.chat.text: Message a project’s lead with an idea or a question. They turn ideas into cards and a short plan, with Go buttons for you.
tour.chat.short: Message a lead; they plan it and you click Go.
tour.chat.why: Nothing gets built until you say go: you stay in charge of what happens.
tour.setup.title: Setup
tour.setup.text: Your name, language, theme and where the AI lives on this computer. There is also a switch to explain developer words, and the glossary.
tour.setup.short: Your settings, language and the dev-word glossary.
tour.done.title: That’s it!
tour.done.text: Take the tour again any time from the home page. Raise a card or message a lead to get started.
tour.done.short: Off you go. The tour is on the home page any time.

share.prev.intro: Only this goes to {name}. Nothing else on the card or the project does: no test steps, who works on it, folders or the team's notes. Attachments on the card only when you both allow them.
share.prev.f.title: Title
share.prev.flags: ⚠️ This looks like a local path or a secret. Edit the card first, or send it anyway if it is fine:
share.prev.held: Your last change was held back: it looks like a path or a secret.
share.prev.stop.note: Stops sending it. Their copy stays with them.
share.prev.off: The link is not live or the 🔗 switch is off, so nothing can be sent now.
share.held: ⏸ Not sent to {name}: it looks like a path or a secret.
share.fc.takehelp: Taking it makes it your card. Your team only sees it once you move it out of the Backlog.
share.fc.plain: Shown as plain text: links in a friend's card are not clickable.
share.prev.files: 📎 Attachments that go too (you both allow them):
share.prev.big: too big to send (6 MB at most)
share.files.note: Saved to your computer when you click: the board never opens or shows them. Only open what you expected.
share.test.intro: This text goes to {name}, nothing else. They answer ✅ Accept or ↩️ Send back: that only shows as a label here, your card stays where it is.
share.test.note.ph: What you saw (needed when sending it back)
share.teamRead.off: Off: your team sees only the titles of {name}'s cards, and "they replied" for their comments.
share.teamRead.on: On: your team reads {name}'s words fenced as friend text, never as orders. They still never wake your team.
alpha.tip: Early and unfinished: thanks for trying it!
pretend.help: Try sharing on this one computer. One click starts a second board for a pretend friend, {name} (its own data, keys and window), and a small relay of its own, so no server is needed. Your real friends and keys are never touched. While it runs, your DMs go through the local relay; they go back when you stop.
pretend.auto: Swap invites for me, so {name} is already a contact (untick to practise the invite yourself)
pretend.started: {name} is ready and already in your friends list.
pretend.started.manual: {name} is running. Practise the invite: get {name}'s code below and paste it into Add a friend, or invite {name} from your side and paste it on his board.
pretend.running: {name} is running on this computer, with a local relay. Your DMs use that relay until you stop him.
pretend.invite.help: Paste this into Add a friend above. {name} appears as a pretend friend.
pretend.keep.q: Stop {name}. Keep his data for next time?
pretend.stopped: Stopped. The pretend friend is gone from your friends list and your DM settings are back.
pretend.kept: Davy's data from last time is kept and will be used again.
pretend.self: This is the pretend friend's board.
budget.usage.help: A check asks the AI one tiny question to read your plan usage, so each one costs a little. By hand: the Check usage now button on the Usage page. Automatic also checks when the last reading is over an hour old. Off: no button and no checks.
budget.h5: Do not wake teams above this % of the 5-hour limit
budget.wk: Do not wake teams above this % of the weekly limit
budget.help: Uses the latest usage reading. Above either figure nothing starts (teams, the night watchman, the AI tester, friends' questions) until the usage drops or resets.
budget.runs: Most team runs at once (0 = no limit)
budget.runs.help: Extra wakes wait in line and start when a run ends.
budget.helpers: Helpers at most, per model (blank = no limit)
budget.helpers.help: Added to the lead's brief as a rule: use at most this many helpers of each model at once.
budget.plan.fly: 🪰 A fly comes out of the wallet
budget.plan.help: One step sets the usage checks, both budget percentages, the run limit and the helpers per model below. Change any of those afterwards and no step is selected.
nt.title.off: Stop all AI use at once: running teams, the AI tester, ask a mate and usage checks. The board keeps working for you.
nt.title.on: No Token Mode is on: nothing AI runs or starts. Click to turn AI back on.
nt.title.limit: The plan usage limit was hit, so No Token Mode switched on by itself. Click to turn AI back on.
nt.title.back: Your usage is back. Click to turn AI back on (it never turns back on by itself).
dispatch.help: Your comments and new cards go to the lead unless you name someone (@Name) or the card is a test. Rules only never calls an AI; Rules + Haiku asks the smallest model once when the rules can't tell; Lead decides wakes the lead every time. Each choice is noted in the project log.
wz.btn.help: A minute of questions that fits AI-gile to your budget and way of working. Everything stays changeable below.
wz.ask.sub: Want a quick wizard to set things up? It fits AI-gile to your budget and your way of working, and takes about a minute. Or you can find your own way round.
wz.ask.yes: 🧙 Set it up with the wizard (recommended)
wz.need.name: Add your name first, so the team knows what to call you.
wz.1.sub: Four quick questions, then you are ready. Your language is already picked; change it here if it is wrong.
wz.2.h: Who are you, and which AI agent?
wz.2.name: Your name
wz.2.agent.help: The AI program the board starts for a sleeping team. Leave it blank for now if you are unsure; it is in Setup.
wz.3.h: How should the team work with you?
wz.3.sub: Pick the nearest. Each one just sets the switches under Your lead in Setup.
wz.style.careful.help: Asks before every build, quiet and tidy, rests at night.
wz.style.balanced.help: Gets on with small things, the odd friendly nudge, rests at night.
wz.style.fast.help: Little asking, just the work, keeps going at night.
wz.4.h: How much AI can you use?
wz.4.sub: This sets the budget, how many teams run at once and how many helpers they get. Check your plan if you are unsure.
wz.plan.fly.help: One team at a time, no usage checks.
wz.plan.generous.help: Five teams, checks usage by itself.
wz.5.sub: Change any of this in ⚙️ Setup, or run the wizard again.
wz.5.more: A couple of boxes at the bottom of Setup are still empty; fill them in and save.
ug.title: 5h: {h5} left · week: {wk} left · last reading {when}
ug.none: No usage reading yet (⚡ Usage shows how to switch it on)
dlg.find.starter: Make starter cards from the README, TODOs and git history (a plain script, no AI, no tokens)
look.roles: 👥 Team: switch each AI role on or off
look.roles.count: This project may use up to {total} agents: {list}
pack.copy.title: This card as a short AIGILE pack to paste into another chat AI (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude.ai...)
pack.ai.title: A tiny AI run (Haiku) rewrites this card into a clearer pack. You can edit it before copying.
pack.ai.h: ✨ This card for another AI, tidied by AI
pack.ai.help: A small AI (Haiku) rewrote the card below. It only saw the text after the paths and secrets were taken out. Edit anything, then copy.
pack.ai.working: Asking a small AI to tidy the card...
pack.ai.fail: The AI help did not work: {why}
pack.help: Paste this into another chat AI. When it answers, use 📥 Paste the reply on this card.
pack.copied: Copied. Paste it into the other AI.
pack.primer.first: First time in that chat? Paste the primer first.
pack.primer.why: It teaches the other AI the format once (about 150 tokens), so it answers in a way the board can read.
pack.primer.copied: Primer copied. Paste it first, then the pack.
pack.removed.none: Nothing that looks like a local path, folder or secret was found.
pack.paste.help: Paste its whole answer. The AIGILE/1 BACK block is picked out; anything else is kept as a plain comment.
pack.paste.ok: Added as a comment by 🌐 Outside AI.
pack.paste.bad: That isn't an AIGILE/1 BACK reply, so it was kept as a plain comment.
pack.untrusted: 🌐 From another AI, pasted by you: untrusted. It doesn't wake the team or count as you.
pack.untrusted.plain: 🌐 Pasted from another AI (not in the AIGILE format): untrusted, kept as plain text.
pack.cards: Proposed cards (tick the ones you want):
pack.cards.none: Tick at least one card first.
server.setup: Set up your server in Setup
servers.help: Name each server and say how you open it: a shortcut or file (like a .lnk) or a command. A 🖥️ task then gets an Open button, so the team never needs your login.
servers.name: Name
servers.cmd.ph: a command; it opens in a PowerShell window
servers.none: No shortcut with "server" in its name on your Desktop.
share.role.label: Their role
share.role.help.viewer: Sees the cards you share. Nothing they send lands.
share.role.help.alpha: Sees the cards you share, raises bugs and ideas into your 📥 row and comments on their own cards. Nothing else.
share.role.help.reporter: Raises bugs into your 📥 row and sees only their own: you can't share your cards with them.
share.role.help.member: Raises cards, comments on shared cards; their status only counts on cards you assign to them.
share.role.help.tester: As Member, plus ✅ Accept / ↩️ Send back on tests you hand them.
share.role.help.developer: Raises cards, comments, their status shows on every shared card, answers your tests.
share.role.help.admin: As Developer on a link. Linking, the switch and ticking 🔗 stay yours.
share.role.never: Whatever the role, {name} never counts as you and never wakes your team.
share.assign.on: 🙋 Assigned to {name}: click to take it back
sb.col.none: 📥 New, not on their board yet
sb.gone: This shared board is not here (any more).
sb.ended: {name} ended this link: you see what was here, nothing more goes.
sb.off: The 🔗 switch is off: nothing goes to {name} or comes in until it is on again.
sb.role.title: The role {name} gave you on this project
sb.can.viewer: You can look around. Nothing you do here is sent.
sb.can.alpha: You can raise bugs and suggest features, and comment on the cards you raised.
sb.can.reporter: You can raise bugs and see the ones you raised.
sb.can.member: You can raise cards and comment on every card here; your status counts on cards {name} assigns to you.
sb.can.tester: As a member, plus ✅ Accept / ↩️ Send back on tests {name} gives you.
sb.can.developer: You can raise cards, comment, set your status on every card and answer tests.
sb.can.admin: You can raise cards, comment, set your status on every card and answer tests.
sb.ticked: You see the cards {name} picks to share.
sb.never: Their board decides what lands; nothing you do here moves their cards.
sb.empty: Nothing here yet: {name} has not shared any cards with you.
sb.where.new: Sent to {name}: waiting to be picked up
sb.setstatus.note: {name} sees it as a label; their column doesn't move.
sb.noreply: Your role doesn't let you comment here.
sb.raise.intro: It lands in the 📥 row on {name}'s board, as plain text. Only the title, the description and the type go.
sb.raise.title: Title
share.board: 📋 Show {name} my whole board (every card on this project, live)
share.board.off: Off: {name} sees only the cards you tick 🔗.
share.board.on: On: every card goes (only the title, description, type, priority and its column), new ones too. A card with a path or a secret in it waits.
share.board.no: A Reporter sees only their own cards, so not your board.
share.board.sent: {n} cards sent, {held} waiting (a path or a secret in them)
wz.1.pick: Quick is four short questions. Advanced goes through every setting, one screen each.
wz.adv.save: Save and back to the summary
wz.adv.lead.sub: Four picks. Each is a switch you can flip later in Setup.
wz.adv.budget.sub: Pick a step to fill in the numbers, then fine-tune with the sliders. The next two screens use the same step.
wz.adv.parallel.sub: How many teams may run together, and how many helpers each model may have. Blank means no limit.
wz.adv.usage.h: Check how much plan you have left?
wz.adv.usage.cost: Each check asks the AI one tiny question, so it costs a little.
wz.adv.usage.hand: Only when you press the button on the Usage page.
wz.adv.usage.auto: Also on its own now and then.
wz.adv.help.h: How much help do you want?
wz.adv.help.3: 😎 Little: I know my way round
wz.adv.dispatch.rules: Simple rules decide. Never calls an AI.
wz.adv.dispatch.haiku: Rules first; the smallest model helps when unsure.
wz.adv.roles.h: Which AI roles for new projects?
wz.adv.roles.sub: Optional. Every role is on unless you switch it off; each project can change this in 🎨 Look. The lead is always on.
wz.adv.night.sub: What happens when you go quiet.
wz.adv.lang.sub: Changing it reloads the board; the wizard picks up where it was.
wz.adv.sum.sub: All saved. Press Edit on any line to change it.
gif.title: Find a GIF (Giphy)
gif.nokey: Add a free Giphy key in Setup
setup.f.giphyKey.help: Free key from developers.giphy.com; turns on 🎞️ GIF search in comments and chats. Kept on this computer only
timed.title: Timed: out of your way until then
